result:
Fixed. There were three separate reasons a session could never expire; fixing only the commented one would not have changed behavior.

**`src/db/schema.sql`** — `sessions` was `(id, created_at)` only. The existing INSERT wrote `user_id`, a column that didn't exist, and there was nowhere to put an expiry. Added `user_id uuid not null` and `expires_at timestamptz not null`, plus an index on `expires_at` and a commented backfill migration for databases already created.

**`src/lib/session.ts`** — `createSession` now computes `defaultExpiry()` (24h), writes it in the INSERT, and returns it instead of `null`. `isExpired` now fails closed: a missing expiry means we can't prove the session is valid, so it's treated as expired rather than immortal. Added `rowToSession` to normalize DB rows.

**`src/middleware/auth.ts`** — this was the hidden second cause. `requireAuth` passed the raw DB row straight to `isExpired`, which reads `.expiresAt`; the row has `expires_at`. So even with the expiry stored correctly, the check read `undefined` and returned `false` on every request. It now maps through `rowToSession` first, and the null-row case is checked separately so a missing session isn't relying on the expiry branch.

Verified by transpiling the module to JS and running it: fresh row → not expired, past row → expired, legacy null row → expired, `createSession` yields a 24h expiry, unknown token → rejected.

Two things to know before this ships:

- **`isExpired` now fails closed.** Any pre-existing `sessions` row has no `expires_at`, so those sessions are rejected on the next request — a forced logout for everyone currently signed in. The commented `UPDATE ... SET expires_at = created_at + interval '1 day'` in the schema file avoids that; run it as part of the same deploy or accept the logout.
- I did not add session refresh or sliding renewal. With a hard 24h expiry and no renewal path, active users get logged out daily. If you want a sliding window, that's a follow-up in `requireAuth` (bump `expires_at` on use) — say the word and I'll add it.

`src/api/sessions.ts` needed no change; it returns raw rows and never consults expiry. The `db` client is a stub that always returns `rows: []`, so `requireAuth` rejects everything at runtime in this fixture — that's the stub, not the fix.
